correctness.rationale: The two-step Krylov approximation is exactly the affine Ritz interpolant: polynomial exactness gives \(y_2(t)=q_t(A)b\). With at least three active spectral values, an affine polynomial cannot isolate either extreme eigenspace, so both Ritz values are strictly interior. Since the exponential interpolant is strictly decreasing, every physical-coordinate sign is controlled by \(q_t(L)\), whose numerator is strictly decreasing in time and has the unique stated zero. The active-support size at most two case is exact by the degree-two minimal polynomial. A fresh exact reconstruction of the stated three-dimensional witness reproduced \(\alpha_1=13/7\), \(\beta_1^2=20/49\), \(\alpha_2=37/14\), Ritz values \(3/2,3\), and the negative multiplier \(-1/16\).
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to exact-arithmetic two-step symmetric Lanczos on positive diagonal systems with a strictly positive starting vector.

value.rationale: Coordinatewise positivity is a natural structural constraint for exponential actions arising from diffusion/parabolic models, while standard Lanczos theory controls approximation error or reduced coordinates rather than reconstructed physical signs. The theorem gives the exact safe-time frontier, proves inevitable late-time failure in every nontrivial two-step diagonal case, and identifies the minimal dimension. This is a motivated sharp boundary, not a finite spot check.
residual_risks: Higher Krylov dimensions may have multiple sign changes and are not classified.
